races.title: State Senate, District 25
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Amy Scott Galey
cands.bio: Republican attorney from Alamance County. UNC-Chapel Hill and UNC School of Law graduate, licensed in NC, SC and DC. Alamance County Commissioner from 2017 and board chair 2017-2020. Elected to the North Carolina Senate in 2020 and now represents District 25.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or the year she moved back to North Carolina from South Carolina. We found no documented position on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, abortion, or immigration and H-1B. Her campaign site describes votes she says she cast, but we did not treat those as verified actions. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her in 2024 or 2026. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so her stated positions come from a 2022 survey and her campaign site. We found no reported controversies.

local.label: Roots 90: She says she was raised in Union Ridge in Alamance County and graduated from Western Alamance High School. She lived in South Carolina for about 10 years before returning to her grandparents' farm, and her birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Practicing attorney and former staff attorney with the Defender Corporation of Charleston County. Alamance County Commissioner from 2017 and board chair 2017-2020. State Senator since 2021, serving on Appropriations, Judiciary and Education committees.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate, local elected office as a county commissioner and board chair, and a legal career. Committee chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate, local elected office as a county commissioner and board chair, and a legal career. Committee chair posts were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she is a strong supporter of the Second Amendment, holds a concealed carry permit and is an NRA member.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: She listed school choice among her key campaign messages, saying nobody should be shut out of the best school for their child because they can't afford it.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she listed protecting lives and property and supporting law enforcement as a key campaign message.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: She says she ran for county commissioner in 2016 out of concern about growth in Alamance County.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: She says she was raised in Union Ridge in Alamance County and graduated from Western Alamance High School. She lived in South Carolina for about 10 years before returning to her grandparents' farm, and her birthplace is not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Describing why she ran for county commissioner, she wrote: "Concerned about the growth in Alamance County, I ran for county commissioner in 2016."

cands.name: Southey Blanton
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 25 in 2026, running against incumbent Republican Amy Galey. No prior elected office is documented in the sources available.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements and voter-guide recommendations from the Center for Freethought Equality, Utility Fairness Now, and several 'Sway' voting groups, including NC Public School Champions, Fair Map Fight Club and Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Southey Blanton was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his job and career history. His campaign site says he was born and raised in North Carolina but gives no detail. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and the pages we could read did not include his issue positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice beyond a general statement of support for public schools. We found no documented public statements on data centers or development, and no controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation, career history or prior office could be found in the pages available.
qual.why: Nothing in the sources establishes his work history, so the score is left empty rather than guessed.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign website calls him a 'Proud supporter of public schools'. This is a general statement and does not address vouchers, charters or teacher pay specifically.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)
